arguments.promptText:
A ten-second naturalistic British comedy advert, filmed as one continuous medium two-shot in a real professional car-detailing bay. Soft side-window daylight, soft white inspection-light reflections, natural skin and believable paint and glass. The reference image anchors the same immaculate cobalt-blue sports coupe, rounded headlights, black split-spoke wheels and grey studio. Keep the clean blue bonnet and both actors' faces clearly readable in the portrait frame.

A fictional female detailer in her thirties, black polo and dark hair tied back, stands beside the car holding its keys. A fictional male customer in his fifties, short grey hair, sage overshirt and grey T-shirt, has come to collect his own car. Ordinary clothes. The owner is affectionate and slightly overprotective of the beautiful finish; he behaves as if his decision is completely reasonable.

The detailer offers the keys slightly forward without a handoff and says: "Your car's ready."
The owner replies calmly: "I'll get a taxi."
The detailer asks, genuinely puzzled: "What about your car?"
The owner gives the plain explanation: "I've just had it cleaned."

Four natural British spoken turns in this exact order, one person speaking at a time, with clearly audible dialogue synchronised to the correct lips. Give the final line its own unhurried beat, lightly stressing "just". Then hold the detailer's small patient reaction and the owner's sincere composure. No grin, wink, laugh or extra line.

Keep the camera steady, both actors and the clean car in one coherent shot. Quiet workshop room tone. No taxi, phone action, getting into the car, key handoff, narrator, music, captions, graphic text or generated logos. This is the complete acted sketch, not a montage.
